questions.question_text: All of the following are true about pharmacodynamics of antipsychotics, except:

options.text: The antipsychotic effect is most closely correlated with the drug's affinity with D 2receptors
The antipsychotic effects may derive from inhibition of dopaminergic neurotransmission in the mesolimbic–cortical tract
The Parkinsonian side-effects derive from inhibition of dopaminergic neurotransmission in the nigrostriatal tract
The endocrine side-effects derive from inhibition of dopaminergic neurotransmission in the tuberoinfudibular tract
The antipsychotic effect of clozapine is correlated with its tendency to occupy 80–100% of D 2receptors

correct_answer.text: The antipsychotic effect of clozapine is correlated with its tendency to occupy 80–100% of D 2receptors

correct_answers.text: The antipsychotic effect of clozapine is correlated with its tendency to occupy 80–100% of D 2receptors

questions.explanation: Mechanism of action of clozapine involves the D 4and 5-HT receptors. In therapeutic concentrations it may occupy only 40–60% of D 2 receptors. Antipsychotic effects are usually obtained when D 2 occupancy is 60–70%.

questions.question_text: The following antipsychotics are correctly matched with their chemical class, except:
questions.explanation: Haloperidol is a butyrophenone and pimozide is a diphenylbutylpiperidine.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about chlorpromazine, except:

options.text: Blockade of a1-adrenoreceptors gives it a sedating profile
Blockade of histamine H 1-receptors gives it a sedating profile
Muscarinic cholinergic receptor blockade produces urinary retention and constipation
Muscarinic cholinergic receptor blockade protects against Parkinsonian symptoms

questions.explanation: Blockade of a1-adrenoreceptors causes hypotension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about antipsychotics?

options.text: Thioridazine is a potent muscarinic antagonist with low incidence of movement disorders
Acute dystonic reaction occurs more commonly with chlorpromazine than with haloperidol
Pimozide is safe in cardiac arrhythmias

correct_answer.text: Thioridazine is a potent muscarinic antagonist with low incidence of movement disorders

correct_answers.text: Thioridazine is a potent muscarinic antagonist with low incidence of movement disorders

questions.explanation: Hyperprolactinaemia is related to D 2receptors; pimozide causes fatal dysrhythmias (torsade de pointes and prolonged QT interval).

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about substituted benzamides, except:

options.text: They are highly selective D 2receptor antagonists
They are more likely to cause sedation

correct_answer.text: They are more likely to cause sedation

correct_answers.text: They are more likely to cause sedation

questions.explanation: Benzamides are not sedative and cause insomnia.

questions.question_text: Risperidone has high affinity to all receptors, except:
questions.explanation: Risperidone is a potent antagonist of both 5-HT 2and dopamine D2receptors.

questions.question_text: All of the following are well known side-effects of risperidone, except:
questions.explanation: Nausea and abdominal pain are the main gastrointestinal side-effects.

questions.question_text: Atypical antipsychotics:

options.text: Are associated with an increased risk of stroke in elderly patients with dementia
May cause tardive dyskinesia on long-term administration
Can cause hyperglycaemia and sometimes diabetes

questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics include substituted benzamides and 5-HT 2–D 2 receptor antagonists.

questions.question_text: Significant interaction occurs between aripiprazole and all the following medications, except:
questions.explanation: The metabolism of aripiprazole is inhibited by fluoxetine and ketoconazole and some antivirals; plasma concentration is reduced by carbamazepine.

questions.question_text: With which of the following are anticholinergic side-effects more common?
questions.explanation: Side-effects include dry mouth, urinary hesitancy and retention, constipation, reduced sweating, blurred vision and precipitation of glaucoma.

questions.question_text: With which of the following does most marked a1blockade occur?
questions.explanation: Side-effects such as sedation and postural hypotension may occur.

questions.question_text: Hyperprolactinaemia commonly occurs in treatment with all antipsychotics, except:
questions.explanation: Hyperprolactinaemia is associated with galactorrhoea, amenorrhoea, low libido and sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: All of the following are common side-effects of clozapine, except:
questions.explanation: Priapism is a rare side-effect of clozapine.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about treatment with clozapine, except:

options.text: It is almost free of extra-pyramidal symptoms (EPS)
It may improve existing tardive dyskinesia (TD)
It causes 95% of agranulocytosis within the first 6 months of treatment
It is indicated in psychosis in Parkinson's disease

questions.explanation: Occurrence of agranulocytosis is approximately 1%.

questions.question_text: Olanzapine:

options.text: Is a stronger receptor antagonist than risperidone
Commonly causes abnormalities of the QT interval

questions.explanation: Olanzapine is a thienobenzodiazepine and quetiapine is a dibenzothiazepine.

questions.question_text: Acute dystonic reaction:

options.text: Occurs later on in long-term treatment with antipsychotics
Is more common in elderly people
Is more likely to occur with chlorpromazine than haloperidol
Can be easily mistaken for histrionic behaviour

correct_answer.text: Can be easily mistaken for histrionic behaviour

correct_answers.text: Can be easily mistaken for histrionic behaviour

questions.explanation: T orticolis, tongue protrusion, grimacing and opisthotonus occur; reaction occurs soon after the treatment and is common in young men; anticholinergic agents control the reaction.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about akathisia, except:

options.text: It usually occurs in the first 2 weeks of antipsychotic treatment
It is reliably controlled by anti-Parkinsonian drugs
Treatment with beta-blockers can be helpful
Treatment with benzodiazepines can be helpful
Reduction in the dose of antipsychotic can be helpful

correct_answer.text: It is reliably controlled by anti-Parkinsonian drugs

correct_answers.text: It is reliably controlled by anti-Parkinsonian drugs

questions.explanation: Akathisia is an unpleasant feeling of physical restlessness and the need to move.

questions.question_text: Among atypical antipsychotics:

options.text: Olanzapine is safe in angle closure glaucoma
Amisulpride is excreted unchanged by the kidney
QT prolongation is a common side-effect of aripiprazole
Sertindole is safe to use in cardiac conduction abnormalities

correct_answer.text: Amisulpride is excreted unchanged by the kidney

correct_answers.text: Amisulpride is excreted unchanged by the kidney

questions.explanation: QT prolongation is a rare side-effect of aripiprazole.

questions.question_text: Among the following antipsychotics, secretion in the breast is lowest with:
questions.explanation: Highly protein-bound compounds secrete less.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Clozapine is safe to give in pregnancy
Galactorrhoea is more common with risperidone than olanzapine
Zotepine is safe in cardiac arrythmias
Anticholinergic drugs should be given regularly to people receiving antipsychotics to reduce side-effects

correct_answer.text: Galactorrhoea is more common with risperidone than olanzapine

correct_answers.text: Galactorrhoea is more common with risperidone than olanzapine

questions.explanation: Clozapine is useful for treating psychotic symptoms of Parkinsonism.

questions.question_text: Parkinsonian side-effects of neuroleptics:

options.text: Occur as a consequence of mesocortical dopamine D 2receptor occupancy
Always appear a few months after the drug has been taken
Do not respond to anti-Parkinsonian treatments
Occur in 90% of patients treated with dopamine receptor antagonists

questions.explanation: Blockade of D 2in the nigrostriatal pathway causes Parkinsonian side-effects of neuroleptics; it occurs in 15% of cases only.

questions.question_text: Parkinsonian side-effects of neuroleptics

options.text: Are more common after the age of 40
May continue after stopping the neuroleptics

questions.explanation: Parkinsonian side-effects are related to the antidopaminergic action on the basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Antipsychotics:

options.text: Are mainly absorbed from the jejunum
Can be used for treating behavioural symptoms of dementia
May cause hypothermia in the elderly

questions.explanation: Antipsychotics except amisulpride are metabolized by the liver.

questions.question_text: Groups at higher risk of tardive dyskinesia include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Unlike other extra-pyramidal side-effects, tardive dyskinesia does not always remit when the drugs are stopped.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of tardive dyskinesia?

options.text: Patients always recover when the neuroleptic is stopped
It is more common in long-term treatment
It occurs in 50% of patients treated with typical neuroleptics
It will not occur in patients treated with atypical antipsychotics
It improves when treated with anticholinergic anti-Parkinsonian drugs

correct_answer.text: It is more common in long-term treatment

correct_answers.text: It is more common in long-term treatment

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia occurs in only 20% of schizophrenics on long-term treatments. Anti-Parkinsonian drugs usually aggravate tardive dyskinesia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of tardive dyskinesia?

options.text: It is characterized by chewing and sucking movements
The limbs and the muscles of respiration may also be involved
It may be seen in patients taking metoclopramide
It is aggravated frequently by stopping the antipsychotic drug

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is occasionally seen in patients who have not taken antipsychotic drugs.

questions.question_text: The clinical picture of neuroleptic malignant syndrome includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Gradual onset of generalized muscular hypertonicity

questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is associated more closely with high-potency antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of neuroleptic malignant syndrome?

options.text: It can be lethal in up to 50% of patients
Risk is decreased in combined lithium and antipsychotic treatment
It will not occur with clozapine
It may cause myoglobinuria, leading to renal failure
Patients who survive usually have residual disability

correct_answer.text: It may cause myoglobinuria, leading to renal failure

correct_answers.text: It may cause myoglobinuria, leading to renal failure

questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is associated with combined lithium and antipsychotic treatment.

questions.question_text: Medications used to treat neuroleptic malignant syndrome include:
questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome treatment is symptomatic: stop the drug; cool the patient; maintain fluid balance; and treat infections.

questions.question_text: Fluoxetine increases the plasma concentration of all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine inhibits few hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes.

questions.question_text: Carbamazepine accelerates the metabolism of:
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine induces hepatic enzymes.

questions.question_text: Anticholinergic anti-Parkinsonian drugs may cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Anticholinergic anti-Parkinsonian drugs may cause constipation.

questions.question_text: Impaired glucose tolerance is associated with:
questions.explanation: All the drugs listed can cause impaired glucose tolerance and weight gain.

questions.question_text: Sexual dysfunction is a side-effect of:
questions.explanation: All these drugs have anti-adrenergic effects, which could cause sexual dysfunction. All the drugs listed could also cause hyperprolactinaemia, resulting in sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: SSRIs are associated with an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleed
Atomoxetine is safe to use in hepatic impairment
Modafenil is used to treat obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome

correct_answer.text: Atomoxetine is safe to use in hepatic impairment

correct_answers.text: Atomoxetine is safe to use in hepatic impairment

questions.explanation: Phenothiazine, haloperidol, quetiapine, olanzapine, risperidone and clozapine could cause SIADH.

questions.question_text: It is reported that in clinical practice the most effective drug for Tourette's syndrome is:
questions.explanation: SSRIs, clonidine, risperidone, etc. are also used in the treatment.

questions.question_text: Regarding drugs used to treat substance misuse problems, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Acamprosate is safe to use in hepatic impairment
Disulfiram is safe to recommend in controlled drinking
Taste disturbance is a rare side-effect of bupropion
In opioid dependence, buprenorphine may precipitate withdrawal reactions due to its partial antagonist properties
Lofexidine is not useful in alleviating symptoms of opioid withdrawal

correct_answer.text: In opioid dependence, buprenorphine may precipitate withdrawal reactions due to its partial antagonist properties

correct_answers.text: In opioid dependence, buprenorphine may precipitate withdrawal reactions due to its partial antagonist properties

questions.explanation: Taste disturbance is a common side-effect of bupropion.

questions.question_text: Features of opioid withdrawal include all of the following, except:

options.text: Fast pulse and raised blood pressure

questions.explanation: Dilated pupils are a feature of opioid withdrawal.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true statements about drugs used in opiate misuse, except:

options.text: Methadone is a synthetic opiate with a high dependency potential and low lethal dose
Lofexidine is a peripherally acting a2-adrenergic antagonist
Naltrexone causes increased sweating and lacrimation
Naloxone is used to reverse neonatal respiratory depression resulting from opioid administration to the mother during labour

correct_answer.text: Lofexidine is a peripherally acting a2-adrenergic antagonist

correct_answers.text: Lofexidine is a peripherally acting a2-adrenergic antagonist

questions.explanation: Lofexidine is a centrally acting a2-adrenergic antagonist.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about pharmacokinetics in ageing, except:

options.text: Total body water and lean body mass increase
Total body fat increases more markedly in women than men
The free or unbound percentage of albumin-bound drugs increases

correct_answer.text: Total body water and lean body mass increase

correct_answers.text: Total body water and lean body mass increase

questions.explanation: Total body water and lean body mass decrease.

questions.question_text: Regarding drugs for dementia:

options.text: Acetylcholinesterase-inhibiting drugs are not useful in dementia associated with Parkinson's disease
Donepezil is an irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor
Galantamine is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase with nicotinic receptor agonist properties
Rivastigmine is a competitive inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase
Memantine is an NMDA receptor agonist

correct_answer.text: Galantamine is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase with nicotinic receptor agonist properties

correct_answers.text: Galantamine is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase with nicotinic receptor agonist properties

questions.explanation: Donepezil is reversible, rivastigmine is non-competitive and memantine is an NMDA antagonist.

questions.question_text: Which of the following anti-dementia medications is safe to use in supraventricular cardiac conduction abnormalities?
questions.explanation: Memantine is not an anticholinesterase; it acts through the NMDA receptor.

questions.question_text: All of the following are antimuscarinic drugs used in Parkinsonism, except:
questions.explanation: Amantadine is a weak dopamine antagonist with modest anti-Parkinsonian effects.

questions.question_text: Common side-effects of levodopa include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Hypersexuality is a rare side-effect.

questions.question_text: Psychosis is a known side-effect of all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Prochlorperazine is used to treat psychosis.

questions.question_text: You are asked to assess a 17-year-old boy brought to the A&E Department by his friends after a party. He is extremely agitated and tells you that 'aliens' are after him and they had put some 'radioactive things' in his body, which he could sense as 'crawling' underneath his skin. On examination he has dilated pupils and tachycardia. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Cocaine bugs (formification) are a feature of cocaine intoxication.

questions.question_text: You are asked to assess a 54-year-old man brought to the A&E Department by paramedics. You found him waiting in front of the A&E help desk believing that it was the local pub. It was reported that he had been wandering near a caravan park early in the morning. On examination he was found to be disorientated in time, and had an ataxic gait. He also had nystagmus and external rectus palsy. The treatment of choice is:
questions.explanation: The most probable diagnosis is Wernicke's encephalopathy as he presented with the symptom triad ataxia–nystagmus–ophthalmoplegia.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about pharmacological effects on the neurophysiology of the brain, except:

options.text: Benzodiazepines decrease REM sleep, stage 3 sleep and stage 4 sleep
Benzodiazepines are associated with REM rebound
Antidepressant and antipsychotic drugs increase delta activity on EEG
Benzodiazepines increase beta activity and decrease alpha activity on EEG
Tricyclic antidepressants suppress REM sleep and increase stage 4 NREM sleep

correct_answer.text: Benzodiazepines are associated with REM rebound

correct_answers.text: Benzodiazepines are associated with REM rebound

questions.explanation: REM sleep is associated with a high level of brain activity.

questions.question_text: Regarding pharmacological agents implicated in sexual dysfunction:

options.text: Dopamine agonists may lead to enhanced erection and libido
Yohimbine is an a2-adrenoreceptor antagonist, used as a treatment for both idiopathic and drug-induced male sexual dysfunction.

questions.explanation: Antipsychotics and SSRIs are associated with sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old man with bipolar disorder had been stable on lithium monotherapy for 5 years. Over the last several months, he has become increasingly withdrawn, with fatigue and poor concentration. He has recently gained weight and complains of constipation. He has developed a dislike of cold and his voice is hoarse. On examination he has bradycardia, dry skin and slowly releasing reflexes. The most probable cause of his problems is:
questions.explanation: Lithium interferes with thyroid hormone production.
